To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

succinimidlyl carbamate derivatives from protected α-amino acids or dipeptides can be used as versatile building blocks for the solid-phase synthesis of oligoureas, ureidopeptides and oligo(ureas/peptides) hybrids.
the succinimidyl ureidopeptide building block (1) can be used for the synthesis of oligoureas and oligourea/peptide hybrids, and that the latter compounds can fold to give a urea turn.

the synthesis and use of succinimidly carbamates from N-protected amino acids and dipeptide derivatives as building blocks for the preparation of ureidopeptides and oligourea/peptide hybrids is reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and conformational analysis of ureido-peptide analogs.
the synthesis of new ureido- and peptidyl-hydantoins as well as the development of novel oligo(ureas/peptides).
the development of new synthetic strategies for the preparation of peptidomimetic structures and the investigation of the structural and conformational properties of the corresponding compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
succinimidylesters 3,4 and 5 are versatile building blocks, which allow the preparation of a variety of ureido-peptide and oligourea/peptide hybrid structures.

the use of the N-Boc protected α-amino acids 1a–1d, 2a–2d and 3a–3d as starting materials is a convenient, efficient and versatile method for the preparation of a variety of succinimidylesters, urea/peptide hybrids and ureidopeptides.
the synthesis of ureidopeptides, peptidylhydantoins, and oligoureas can be achieved from the succinimidyl derivatives 4 and 5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

succinimidly carbamates are versatile building blocks for the preparation of a variety of ureido‐containing compounds, such as ureidotripeptides, ureido‐peptides, peptidyl‐hydantoins, and urea‐containing oligomers, which are of interest for the development of conformationally‐constrained peptidomimetics and for the preparation of oligomers with novel structural features.

the synthesis of ureidopeptides and oligourea/peptide hybrids from N-protected α-aminoisobutyric acid and dipeptides can be accomplished in a straightforward way by means of a simple, two-step protocol, and that the resulting ureido-peptides and oligoureas are conformationally flexible in both [D6]dichloromethane and [D6]-dimethylsulfoxide.
we have developed an easy and efficient method to prepare succinimidyl N-protected α-amido carbamates 4 and 5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ureido-peptides, peptidylhydantoins and oligourea/peptide hybrids are readily accessible by the use of succinimidlyl carbamates as building blocks.

the synthesis of ureidotripeptides 6 and 7, peptidylhydantoins 9 and 11 and ureidotripeptide pentamer 10 was achieved with good to excellent overall yields, and that the conformation of the oligoureas in solution is influenced by the nature of the N-protecting group and the solvent.
the use of the ureido moiety in peptide chemistry is a promising tool for the synthesis of constrained peptide mimetics.
